assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin action, proglucagon processing, stable agonists) has produced therapies that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with broad cardiometabolic benefit. The discovery chain from hormone biology to drug is clear and the impact is very large.
assessment.attribution: Drucker and Holst defined GLP-1 biology and its therapeutic rationale; Mojsov's contribution on the active peptide form is substantial but her credit relative to others (for example Habener, who is not in the supplied credit list) is contested as far as I recall. Knudsen is an industrial drug-development contributor; with a three-person cap she is excluded.
assessment.maturity: Clinical confirmation is extensive and independent across multiple trials and agents; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit for the peptide identification and early work is disputed and I cannot verify the details independently.
The three-person cap forces exclusion of the pharmaceutical development contribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provided a general method to control defined cell types with light, reshaping neuroscience and physiology and enabling circuit-level causal tests. The originality and methodological reach are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery and characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) and its deployment in neurons and circuits (Deisseroth, Boyden; Miesenböck's earlier genetically targeted photoactivation) form a multi-party chain. Choosing Nagel, Hegemann and Deisseroth is one defensible configuration, but it leaves out Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated for over a decade and used across fields; early clinical use (retinal optogenetics) is emerging. Timing is mature.
uncertainties: Six credited people and a three-laureate limit make fair allocation difficult.
Whether the prize should reward the molecular tool or the neuroscience application is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new mode of organelle-to-nucleus signaling and proteostasis control, relevant to diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. The concept is clear, original and foundational.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently identified the central Ire1/Hac1 (XBP1) signaling pathway and the mechanism of its activation; a two-person prize is coherent. Other contributors (for example Ron on the integrated stress response) are not in the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is well confirmed in yeast and mammals over many years; therapeutic translation is still developing, but the basic science is mature.
uncertainties: Clinical translation is less settled than the basic mechanism.
Overlap with the related integrated stress response could complicate scope.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR defined the central regulator of cell growth and nutrient sensing, with consequences for cancer, metabolism, immunosuppression and aging. Importance and lasting impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR genetically and established its role in growth control; Schreiber's work on the FKBP12-rapamycin complex helped identify the target pharmacologically. Sabatini's work on mTORC1 nutrient sensing is significant, but the three-person cap and uncertainty about credit make a Hall-and-Schreiber configuration cleaner. Rapamycin's discovery (not credited here) is also part of the story.
assessment.maturity: Strongly and independently confirmed; the pathway is a cornerstone of cell biology, though some clinical applications (aging) remain unproven.
uncertainties: Credit among Hall, Schreiber, Sabatini and the rapamycin discoverers is unresolved.
Hall-and-Schreiber captures only part of the pathway's later development.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered CAR-T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new class of living therapeutic. The impact on cancer immunotherapy is large and clear.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain led the design and clinical translation of costimulatory-domain CAR constructs; Rosenberg contributed to adoptive cell therapy more broadly and early clinical CAR work. The foundational chimeric-receptor concept (Eshhar and others) is not in the supplied credits, which weakens the configuration.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and years of follow-up; solid tumours and toxicity remain open, but the hematologic effect is well established.
uncertainties: Unrepresented early pioneers of the chimeric receptor concept limit fairness.
Overlap with recently recognized immunotherapy prizes may affect priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense correction of SMN2 splicing led to nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, and showed that splicing modulation can be a clinical modality. This ties RNA processing mechanism to a striking clinical outcome.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and target sequences; Bennett led the antisense oligonucleotide chemistry and drug development. A two-person prize is coherent, though Ionis and collaborators beyond them contributed.
assessment.maturity: Approved in 2016 with long clinical follow-up and independent replication; the broader platform is still maturing.
uncertainties: Whether the advance is judged as a single therapy or a platform is uncertain.
Other contributors to the oligonucleotide chemistry are not credited here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of BCL11A as the fetal-to-adult hemoglobin switch regulator led to the first approved CRISPR-based therapy for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia. It joins human genetics, regulatory biology and curative treatment.
assessment.attribution: Orkin and Sankaran established BCL11A's role; Bauer contributed the enhancer-targeting strategy that enabled the therapy. Thein's contribution to the genetic association work is relevant but the three-person cap excludes her.
assessment.maturity: Therapy was approved recently, so long-term durability data are limited; the mechanistic basis is well confirmed.
uncertainties: Long-term safety and durability are not yet established.
The cap forces exclusion of Thein, and the CRISPR editing technology itself was recognized separately.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Chaperonin-assisted folding showed that proteins can fold with machinery assistance in the cell, a foundational principle for protein homeostasis with relevance to neurodegeneration and disease.
assessment.attribution: Horwich and Hartl jointly demonstrated the chaperonin (Hsp60/GroEL) mechanism in mitochondria and in vitro; the pairing is natural, though other pioneers (for example Ellis on the chaperone concept) exist and are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed, with textbook status for decades; recognition is fully mature and arguably late.
uncertainties: Its fit within Physiology or Medicine rather than Chemistry may be debated.
Direct medical impact is less immediate than for the therapeutic candidates.
